sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale chestnut brown, the nasus darker (except at the tip), the head grass yellow in some individuals (immature?); head deeply constricted, the shape of the head and nasus similar to Constrictotermes incisus, but head and body longer, broader and thicker; head widest at the base, forming an angle with the thorax. Head hairs and setae as in C. incisus. Ventral surface of the head slightly paler. Antennae yellowish brown, 13 segments, covered with short hairs: segment 1 long, cylindrical, thick; segment 2 short, rather slender, cylindrical, less than half as long as segment 1; segment 3 clavate, long, slender at the base, 2 times as long as segment 2; segment 4 equal to segment 2; segment 5 shorter than segment 3; terminal segment long, slender, nearly oval. Pronotum pale yellowish brown, saddle-shaped, broader than long, longer than in incisus, the anterior region covered with short hairs, the anterior and lateral margins with a few long setae. Mesonotum and metanotum concolorous, longer than in incisus. Dorsal abdomen slightly darker (grey), the ventral surface paler; abdomen covered with long golden yellow hairs. Legs pale yellow, long and slender. Measurements: soldier total length 3.25—3.85 mm; head length including nasus 1.40—1.50 mm; head length (excluding nasus) 0.75—1.0 mm; nasus length 0.45—0.50 mm; combined length of abdomen and thorax 2.10—2.70 mm; pronotum length 0.105—0.107 mm; hind tibia length 0.808—1.10 mm; head width 0.60—0.64 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Originally published as Constrictotermes (Tenuirostritermes) briciae. Type locality British Honduras (Belize); type specimen USNM No. 24575. The original noted that this species, like incisus, is known from only one soldier morph.
